title: Coordinate cup products compute trivial discrete-lattice derived invariants
statement:
Let $R$ be any commutative condensed ring on the small coherent profinite site [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention], and use ordinary internal module derived categories [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $r\geq0$ and let $D=\mathbf Z^r$ with the discrete topology, acting trivially on $R$ [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. For $1\le i\le r$ let $d_i:\underline D\to(R,+)$ be the additive condensed map induced sectionwise by $(n_1,\ldots,n_r)\mapsto n_i1_R$. Write $\delta_i:R[-1]\to R\Gamma_{R,D}(R[0])$ for its connecting character class, using the cup product and the connecting-class normalization of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus].

Let $\mathcal E_{R,r}=\bigoplus_{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}}R[-|I|]$, represented by the zero-differential complex whose degree $q$ term is the finite sum indexed by $q$-element subsets. The morphism
$$\chi_{R,r}:\mathcal E_{R,r}\longrightarrow R\Gamma_{R,D}(R[0])$$
which is the unit on $I=\varnothing$ and $\delta_{i_1}\smile\cdots\smile\delta_{i_q}$ on the summand for $I=\{i_1<\cdots<i_q\}$ is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_R)$. This specifies the actual derived morphism, including its cup-product normalization. For $r=0$ it is the identity $R[0]$. The zero ring is allowed; no characteristic, completeness, or flatness assumption on $R$ is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution] to $P=R$ with trivial action. Use [lem-sfb-lattice-ordered-koszul-products] to identify its zero-differential complex $K_R(R;1)$, with the specified inclusions $u_I$, with $\mathcal E_{R,r}$. Choose the simultaneous comparison $\lambda$ of [lem-sfb-lattice-koszul-triangulated-cup-comparison]. Its component $\lambda_R$ is an isomorphism and sends the empty-subset inclusion to the canonical derived unit.

source.place: Paragraph (3), algebraic dense-lattice input; agent assembly step 1, after the 2026-10-22 work-spreading re-split.

proof.text: For every $i$, apply [lem-sfb-lattice-character-koszul-boundary] with this same $\lambda$. It supplies the exact unipotent extension, its underlying degreewise splitting and its positive derived singleton boundary, and gives $\delta_i=\lambda_R\circ Q(u_{\{i\}})$ as derived morphisms.

source.place: Paragraph (3), algebraic dense-lattice input; agent assembly step 2, after the 2026-10-22 work-spreading re-split.

proof.text: The pairing compatibility of [lem-sfb-lattice-koszul-triangulated-cup-comparison] applies to $B=R$: $R\otimes_R-$ is the identity, so its flatness hypothesis holds. By [lem-sfb-lattice-ordered-koszul-products], multiplying the increasingly ordered singleton inclusions yields $u_I$, including the empty unit, under the specified shift-tensor identifications. Substitute step 2 and the pairing equality at each product. Thus the prescribed ordered cup on every summand $I$ equals $\lambda_R\circ Q(u_I)$, with coefficient $+1$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), algebraic dense-lattice input; agent assembly step 3, after the 2026-10-22 work-spreading re-split.

proof.text: The finite biproduct universal property now gives $\chi_{R,r}=\lambda_R$, hence invertibility. For $r=0$, [lem-sfb-lattice-ordered-koszul-products] identifies the sole empty summand with $R[0]$, and [lem-sfb-lattice-koszul-triangulated-cup-comparison] normalizes the comparison to the identity. For the zero ring all terms are zero objects and the unique morphism is their identity. The computations divide by no integer and impose no further coefficient hypothesis.
